A ring shaped tube contains two ideal gases with equal masses
and atomic mass numbers M_1­=32 and M_2=28. The gases are separated by
one fixed partition X and another movable conducting partition Y which
can move freely without friction inside the ring. The angle is $\alpha$,

$\therefore\frac{V_{1}}{n_{1}} = \frac{V_{2}}{n_{2}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{360 - \alpha}{n_{1}} = \frac{\alpha}{n_{2}}$
$\left( \therefore V_{1} = (360 - \alpha)rA \right.\ $ and $V_{2} = \alpha rA$
$\Rightarrow M_{1}(360 - \alpha) = M_{2}\alpha\lbrack\therefore n_{1} = \frac{m}{M_{1}}andn_{2} = \frac{m}{M_{2}}\rbrack$
$\alpha = \frac{360M_{1}}{M_{1} + M_{2}} = 192^{\circ}$
